text:
maria: quick heads-up — we're seeing a p99 latency bump on L40S for the short-seq workload (seq=32) vs A100/H100. not huge but consistent across yesterday's nightly runs. can someone run a quick cross-sku check?

kai: thanks for flagging. do we have the failing job id or commit?

maria: job id 2026-03-16-l40s-shortseq in bench infra. linked traces look like more CPU-side queuing before CUDA launch. also noticed higher memcpy times.

sam: I can spin a 3-run sweep (A100 / H100 / L40S) later today. which model + config? small transformer_v2 with batch=8, seq=32, temp=0.0.

maria: exact run: model=redwood/rv2-small@v1.2, bs=8, seq=32, kv=false (same as production). here's the quick runner we use: 
```
./bench/run_compare.sh --model redwood/rv2-small@v1.2 \
  --batches 100 --batch-size 8 --seq 32 \
  --savings-tag shortseq-quick \n```

emma: FYI L40S hosts in lab hit thermal throttling if you run >1200 tokens/s sustained on that node. add a --thermal-tag to isolate if you need longer runs.

sam: noted. i'll set --thermal-tag=l40s-lab and keep runs to 3x100 batches. starting in ~30m.

bench-bot: created bench job 1991234601 for sam: cross-sku-shortseq (A100,H100,L40S) — queued on infra-priority-2. link: https://bench.internal/jobs/1991234601

kai: if you see memcpy spike, try enabling our attn-opt and compare with/without KV cache enabled. flags: `--attn-opt on|off`, `--kv-cache on|off`. also capture nvprof on one run.

sam: running with `--attn-opt on` and `--kv-cache off` for first pass. will capture `ncu` profile on the L40S run.

maria: ping me once you have initial numbers. if L40S still worse we'll triage kernel fallback or driver mismatch.

sam: quick preliminary numbers (3 runs each):
A100 p50/ p95/ p99 = 18ms / 28ms / 42ms
H100 p50/ p95/ p99 = 17ms / 26ms / 40ms
L40S p50/ p95/ p99 = 19ms / 36ms / 68ms
L40S has ~70% higher p99 vs H100.

kai: thanks. can you paste logs for memcpy times and any `kernel fallback` warnings? also which driver/kernel version on L40S?

sam: logs show memcpy spikes around 12-18ms in the critical window. no explicit "kernel fallback" lines but one warning: `quant-kernel: using slow-path matmul` twice. driver on L40S: 530.41.02, CUDA 12.2.

emma: 530.xx drivers are fine but older micropatches matter. L40S nodes were on a different microcode image last week; I'll check node config.

maria: action items: (1) sam to re-run with `--kv-cache on` and `--attn-opt off` to see if memcpy shifts, (2) kai to review ncu from L40S for host-to-device stalls, (3) emma to confirm L40S node firmware/driver micropatch parity.

sam: starting second sweep now with `--kv-cache on` and ncu capture. will also tag thermal.

bench-bot: job 1991234680 created for sam (variant: kv-on, attn-off).

sam: interim result (kv on): L40S p99 down to 46ms, p95 30ms. memcpy spikes largely reduced. looks like KV changed memory access pattern and cut memcpy.

kai: that's promising — suggests path diff rather than pure kernel perf. i'll deep-dive NVTX timeline later and check for CPU serialization.

emma: L40S nodes confirmed on older microcode; rolling the micropatch today evening. will note in infra changelog.

maria: great. schedule 15-min sync if kai needs to walk through nvprof/ncu. otherwise we'll close as "investigate further if reappears". thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

sam: :thumbsup: will drop full logs in #eng-runtime-artifacts and update the bench ticket 1991234601.

kai: +1, please include the exact `ncu` command you used.

sam: `ncu --target-processes all --set full --output l40s_shortseq.ncu`

maria: closing notes: likely root cause = memory access pattern (KV off) + microcode mismatch. re-open if p99 regresses after micropatch.
